newsitem.title: GERMANY: DBKom will be profitable in 5 yrs - German railway.
newsitem.headline: DBKom will be profitable in 5 yrs - German railway.

text.p: DBKom, the telecommunications subsidiary of German railway Deutsche Bahn AG, will become profitable in five years and will invest two to three billion marks in that period, Deutsche Bahn said on Saturday.

The subsidiary, in which a consortium led by Mannesmann AG recently bought a stake of 49.8 percent, should reach a market share of eight percent by the year 2005, Deutsche Bahn chief financial officer Diethelm Sack told Boersen-Zeitung newspaper in an interview.
DBKom's sales will have risen tenfold to at least 10 billion marks by then, Sack said.
At present only 4,000 kilometres of DBKom's 40,000 kilometre line network consisted of optical fibre cables, Sack said.
"To be able to do decent business we need 10,000 kilometres of optical fibre cable," the newspaper quoted him as saying.
Sack said the Mannesmann-led consortium would pay the one billion-mark price for its stake in three instalments by mid-1997.
The sale would generate extraordinary earnings of 400 million marks which the railway would spend on infrastructure, Sack said.
Mannesmann holds 70 percent of the consortium that bought the DBKom stake. The group also includes AT&T and European telecoms venture Unisource NV, each with 15 percent.

As part of the purchase, Mannesmann is merging its CNI unit with DBKom, creating Germany's second-largest telecommunications carrier after Deutsche Telekom, with annual sales of over one billion marks ($663.2 million)
